definition: Keras is an open-source library that provides a Python interface for artificial neural networks.
details: Keras was first independent software, then integrated into the TensorFlow library, and later added support for more. "Keras 3 is a full rewrite of Keras [and can be used] as a low-level cross-framework language to develop custom components such as layers, models, or metrics that can be used in native workflows in JAX, TensorFlow, or PyTorch — with one codebase." Keras 3 will be the default Keras version for TensorFlow 2.16 onwards, but Keras 2 can still be used.

explainer.lead: How to install Keras, a first working example, and where it fits in an AI project.
explainer.createdBy: Created by François Chollet (2015); developed at Google.

install.python: pip install keras          # plus a backend: jax, torch or tensorflow

quickstart.python:
import os
os.environ["KERAS_BACKEND"] = "jax"   # or "torch" / "tensorflow"
import keras

model = keras.Sequential([
    keras.layers.Input((28 * 28,)),
    keras.layers.Dense(128, activation="relu"),
    keras.layers.Dense(10, activation="softmax"),
])
model.compile(optimizer="adam", loss="sparse_categorical_crossentropy", metrics=["accuracy"])
model.summary()

explainer.inAi: Keras 3 is backend-agnostic, so one model definition runs on JAX, PyTorch or TensorFlow. KerasHub ships ready pretrained models such as Gemma.
explainer.jsNote: Python only. The TensorFlow.js Layers API (@tensorflow/tfjs) is modelled on Keras and can load Keras models.
